Puto Bumbong

Served at: Gaudete Sunday

Serves 4-6Prep 20 minCook 15 min

Puto Bumbong is a beloved Filipino steamed rice cake, distinctively purple and traditionally cooked in bamboo tubes. It's a quintessential treat during the Christmas season in the Philippines, especially enjoyed after attending Simbang Gabi (dawn masses), which includes Gaudete Sunday. Its warm, slightly sweet, and chewy texture, topped with butter, shredded coconut, and muscovado sugar, makes it a comforting and festive holiday staple.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (240 g) glutinous rice flour (preferably purple glutinous rice flour or mixed with 1/2 tsp ube powder for color)
  • 1 cup (240 mL) water
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter or margarine, softened
  • 1/2 cup (40 g) freshly grated coconut
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) muscovado sugar (or dark brown sugar)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour (and ube powder, if using) and salt. Gradually add water, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. The dough should be moist but not sticky.
  2. Divide the dough into small, log-like pieces, about 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm) long and 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thick.
  3. Prepare your steamer. If you have a traditional puto bumbong steamer with bamboo tubes, use that. Otherwise, line a regular steamer basket with banana leaves or parchment paper.
  4. Arrange the dough pieces in the prepared steamer, ensuring they are not overcrowded. Steam for 5-7 minutes, or until they are soft, chewy, and cooked through.
  5. Carefully remove the steamed puto bumbong from the steamer.
  6. While still hot, brush each piece generously with softened butter or margarine.
  7. Arrange the puto bumbong on a plate. Sprinkle generously with grated coconut and muscovado sugar.
  8. Serve immediately and enjoy warm.

Tips

  • For an authentic purple color, look for 'pirurutong' glutinous rice flour or add a small amount of ube powder to regular glutinous rice flour.
  • If you don't have a bamboo steamer, a regular steamer basket lined with banana leaves or parchment paper works well. Banana leaves impart a subtle aroma.
  • Adjust the amount of butter, coconut, and sugar to your personal preference. Some also like a drizzle of condensed milk for extra sweetness.
